message.reasoning:
We need to produce JUnit 4 test class for W3CDom.

First extract public methods: fromJsoup(Document), convert(Document, Document), asString(Document). Also maybe constructors? default constructor is implicit public. Also inner class W3CBuilder is protected static, not public.

List signatures:

public Document fromJsoup(org.jsoup.nodes.Document in)

public void convert(org.jsoup.nodes.Document in, Document out)

public String asString(Document doc)

Now generate basic test cases checking functionality.

Need to use jsoup library to create a jsoup Document. Since we don't have external dependencies in test environment? Usually we can add jsoup as dependency. Assume it's available.

Test fromJsoup: create simple HTML, parse with Jsoup.parse, then call fromJsoup, verify returned Document is not null, root element name matches, maybe check namespace handling? Basic.

Test convert: create jsoup Document, create empty W3C Document via DocumentBuilderFactory, call convert, verify modifications (root element present). Use builder.

Test asString: create simple W3C Document with an element, call asString, ensure result contains XML string representation (e.g., "<test/>").

Edge cases: fromJsoup null input should throw NullPointerException (Validate.notNull). Validate class? Not imported, but likely jsoup's internal Validate class throws IllegalArgumentException? Actually Validate.notNull throws IllegalArgumentException. We'll test that.

asString with Document that causes TransformerException? Hard to simulate; maybe pass null doc should throw NullPointerException? Actually transformer.transform with null source may NPE; we can test null leads to IllegalStateException.

convert with jsoup document having empty location (null or empty) ensures documentURI not set. Also test namespace handling: element with xmlns attribute, ensure namespace URI preserved.

Edge cases: attribute names with invalid characters should be stripped.

Also test comment conversion: ensure comment nodes appear.

Potential exceptions: fromJsoup ParserConfigurationException is caught and rethrown as IllegalStateException; we cannot force that easily without mocking factory to throw, but we can simulate by using a custom DocumentBuilderFactory that throws? Too complex. We'll skip.

Now write test methods.

We'll need imports: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Assert.*, org.jsoup.Jsoup, org.jsoup.nodes.Document (jsoup), org.w3c.dom.Document, org.w3c.dom.Element, org.w3c.dom.Comment, etc.

Create test class W3CDomTest with @Test methods.

Test methods naming: testFromJsoupBasic, testFromJsoupNullInput, testConvertBasic, testConvertNamespace, testConvertAttributesFiltering, testAsStringBasic, testAsStringNullDocument.

Implementation details:

- For namespace test: create HTML like "<root xmlns=\"http://example.com\"><child>text</child></root>" using Jsoup.parse with XML parser? Use Jsoup.parse(String html, String baseUri, org.jsoup.parser.Parser.xmlParser()) to preserve namespaces. Jsoup's XML parser retains attribute names as they are. Then after conversion, check that root element's namespaceURI equals "http://example.com". The W3C Document's root element namespace should be set accordingly.

- For attribute filtering: create element with attribute "invalid!key" = "value". After conversion, attribute should be omitted or sanitized. According to copyAttributes, key is sanitized by removing characters not allowed, then matches pattern. So "invalid!key" becomes "invalidkey"? Actually replaceAll removes any character not in allowed set; "!" removed, resulting "invalidkey". That matches pattern, so attribute will be set as "invalidkey". So test that attribute name is sanitized.

- For comment: include comment in HTML: "<!-- comment -->". After conversion, ensure W3C document contains a comment node as child of root.

Implementation for retrieving nodes: root = out.getDocumentElement(); then root.getFirstChild() etc.

Now produce final test file with markers.
